title: Capacity skiplist: headcount lattice with price fallbacks
summary: Working sheet to model a "skiplist" approach to capacity commitments: staggered headcount/hire lanes + financial buffers + explicit price-fallback triggers for hosted API slabs. Purpose: generate quick-turn sensitivity outputs to inform near-term hiring and temporary reserve funding decisions.
assumptions: committed GPU bucket: 40% reserved, 30% dedicated reserve, 30% spot/burst
price elasticity: -0.6 demand vs unit price (short window)
KV cache and batching expected to reduce token spend by 7% in baseline
scenario_summaries: Constrained spot (spot price spike +30%): rely on skiplist -> postpone Lane B hires by 6 weeks; use contractors to cover immediate load; runway impact ~ -$120k over 90 days.

Aggressive growth +30%/mo: need to accelerate committed GPU purchases; recommended take 2 additional reserved units in Oct; incremental headcount must be converted from contractors to perm faster (45-60 days).

Price compression event (-20% across market): revenue per token drops ~20%; offset by 9% cost reduction from quantization recommendations; still requires temporary hiring freeze for non-critical roles unless token growth > 25% QoQ.
sensitivity_results: Most sensitive lever: committed GPU mix vs spot exposure — 5% change in spot availability shows up as ~3.4% variance in monthly burn.
Headcount phasing: moving 1 full-time perm hire from Sep->Nov reduces 90d burn by ~$150k but increases risk for SLA breaches under scenario 'Aggressive growth'.
Pricing elasticity modeled: small price increases (up to +6%) reduce demand nonlinearly; recommended incremental pricing tests limited to +3% in pilots.
